newsitem.title: USA: Companies deny Boeing pressuring Northrop on Airbus.
newsitem.headline: Companies deny Boeing pressuring Northrop on Airbus.

text.p: Boeing Co. and Northrop Grumman Corp. both denied on Friday that Boeing was pressuring Northrop not to work on rival Airbus Industrie's planned super-jumbo jetliner.

"Boeing cannot preclude its suppliers from doing business with any other company," Boeing spokeswoman Sherry Nebel said in response to reports in Europe that the Seattle aircraft maker was pressuring U.S. suppliers not to work with Airbus.
Los Angeles-based Northrop, a major sub-contractor for Boeing, also denied the allegation.
"(After) we made a decision not to be in the nacelles design and integration business ... the foundation for working with Airbus was no longer there," said Georgia Engle, a spokeswoman for Northrop.
"We are not working with them," she added.

Airbus had been in exploratory talks with Northrop over supplying engine housing sections, known as nacelles, for the so-called A3XX super-jumbo, but the talks ended when Northrop opted to exit the engine housing business.
The European consortium has been looking for partners to share up to 40 percent of the expected $10 billion in development costs for the A3XX, which would seat 550 passengers in the basic version.

Newspapers quoted Daimler-Benz Aerospace Chairman Manfred Bischoff as saying Thursday that he was concerned Boeing and merger partner McDonnell Douglas Corp. were trying to induce a big U.S. subcontractor -- understood to be Northrop -- not to work on the Airbus project.
Airbus Industrie, however, said Friday that it had no evidence that archrival Boeing was putting pressure on U.S. suppliers to prevent them from working on the Airbus super-jumbo.
"We have no evidence of any kind of pressure," an Airbus spokesman said.

However, an industry source close to Airbus said Boeing had put pressure on Northrop to stay out of the A3XX project, which threatens Boeing's lucrative monopoly in the high-capacity aircraft segment with its 747 jumbo.
"It is a fact," the source said.
Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a subsidiary of Daimler-Benz AG of Germany, is a partner in Airbus Industrie along with France's Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc and Casa of Spain.
